# Settle Up CLI

> Open-source, MIT-licensed command-line tool for Settle Up. Designed for people and shell-capable AI agents. This is a CLI, not an MCP server.

## Install

Requires Node.js 22 or newer.

npm install -g settle-up-cli

Command name: settleup. Production endpoints are included; no Firebase API key or backend setup is required.

## Authentication

Ask the user to run `settleup auth login` in their own terminal. Email/password only. Google, Apple and other sign-in users should first visit https://settleup.app/migrate-account to migrate to email/password. Never request passwords or session tokens in an agent conversation. Never read local auth files. The CLI refreshes tokens automatically.

## Agent workflow

1. `settleup --help` for command discovery.
2. `settleup auth status` for local session presence.
3. `settleup groups list` and `settleup members list --group-id <groupId>` to resolve exact IDs.
4. Use read commands to inspect transactions and debts.
5. `settleup schema expenses.create` (or another write operation) before constructing a JSON payload.
6. Perform only user-authorized writes with exact IDs and `--input <file.json>` or stdin via `--input -`.
7. Read back the result. Never blindly retry a create operation after an uncertain response.

Stdout is JSON: `{ "ok": true, "data": ..., "meta": ... }` or `{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": ..., "message": ..., "details": ... }, "meta": ... }`. Errors have nonzero exit codes. Account uid and group memberId differ; payments and splits use memberId. Amounts and weights are decimal strings. Write dates are epoch milliseconds. Patches preserve omitted fields; supplied arrays and objects replace their stored fields in full.
